strings: Deep within Thistlefur Hold in northern Ashenvale, a caged bear named Ruul awaits rescue from the corrupted Thistlefur furbolgs. Horde adventurers can assist the captive in fighting his way out of the furbolg den to safety.

While venturing into the corrupted woods of northern Ashenvale, the druid Ruul Snowhoof wandered too close to Thistlefur Hold while in his bear form. The corrupted furbolgs, lacking their ancestral wisdom and driven by feral paranoia, mistook the shapeshifted tauren for a common beast. Rather than treating him with reverence, they caged and starved him, sapping his magical reserves and leaving him unable to break free on his own.

Weakened by hunger and imprisonment, Ruul cannot shift forms or fight through the cavernous furbolg settlement unassisted. Once freed by an ally of the Horde, he relies on his rescuer to clear a path past waves of hostile Thistlefurs. Upon safely reaching the outskirts of Splintertree Post, he briefly reveals his true tauren form to offer heartfelt thanks before returning to the wilderness to sleep off his exhaustion.
Why was Ruul Snowhoof locked up by the furbolgs?

Ruul was exploring the forests in his bear form. The corrupted Thistlefur furbolgs failed to recognize him as a druid, mistaking him for a wild beast, and locked him in a cage where they starved him until he lacked the strength to escape.
why is ruul trapped | how did ruul get captured | why caged
Yama Snowhoof is Ruul's sister, stationed at Splintertree Post in Ashenvale. She had grown deeply worried after Ruul disappeared into the forest days earlier without returning.
ruul sister | yama splintertree | who is yama
Why couldn't Ruul just shift out of bear form to escape?

The prolonged captivity and deliberate starvation inflicted by the Thistlefur furbolgs left Ruul severely weakened. Without food and strength, his reserves of natural energy were completely depleted, leaving him helpless until rescued.
why didnt ruul shapeshift | druid bear trap
What happens after Ruul reaches safety?

Once escorted out of the hostile den to the borders of Splintertree Post, Ruul briefly shifts into his natural tauren form to express his gratitude before retreating back into bear form to find a quiet place to sleep and recover.
where does ruul go | ruul ending
Are all furbolgs in Ashenvale hostile like the Thistlefurs?

No. While many furbolg tribes possess a noble heritage and deep ties to nature, the Thistlefurs of northern Ashenvale have succumbed to dark, corruptive influences that have turned them aggressive and unpredictable.
Where does the rescue take place?
Ruul is imprisoned inside Thistlefur Hold, a furbolg den located in the hills northwest of Splintertree Post and north of Astranaar in Ashenvale.
where is ruul | ruul snowhoof location
ashenvale | druid escort | furbolg | ruul snowhoof | splintertree post | thistlefur hold | yama snowhoof
Ruul's capture is a humbling reminder of the risks of wandering feral territories in animal guise, where corrupted locals cannot tell friend from quarry.
Every soul rescued from the corrupted hollows of northern Ashenvale strengthens the Horde's precarious outpost at Splintertree Post.
Rescuing a stranded brother of the Cenarion circle and easing the worries of his kin at Splintertree Post honors the bonds of the Earthmother and the Horde.
Why does Ruul Snowhoof need you to escort him rather than escaping on his own?

Ruul has spent days trapped inside a Thistlefur cage, enduring starvation and captivity at the hands of the corrupted furbolgs. His physical strength has almost completely failed him. Weakened, malnourished, and trapped deep inside the hostile Thistlefur Hold, he cannot fight his way past the surrounding tribe alone and relies on you to carve a path to freedom.

This errand marks the opening step in unraveling the covert syndicate terrorizing Westfall. Dispatched by Gryan Stoutmantle of Sentinel Hill, travelers are directed eastward into Redridge to consult a shady contact who might know where the thieves hide.

Westfall has descended into ruin, stripped of its harvests and overrun by bandits wearing red bandanas. Gryan Stoutmantle and the People's Militia hold Sentinel Hill against near-constant harassment, yet they fight in the dark. Stoutmantle realizes that hacking away at stray looters will never save the region without finding the cartel's inner circle and identifying who commands them.

Rather than relying on official military channels or Stormwind's absentee nobles, Stoutmantle turns to his personal debts. He sends trusted adventurers past Elwynn into the Redridge Mountains. In the quiet lakeside village of Lakeshire, lurking on the upper floor of the local inn, sits a rogue named Wiley the Black. Knowing the underworld far better than any militia captain, Wiley represents the first thread in unraveling the Brotherhood's hideouts.

Gryan Stoutmantle is the leader of the People's Militia, a ragtag defense force stationed at Sentinel Hill in Westfall. With Stormwind neglecting the borderlands, he coordinates the defense of the few remaining local farmers and refugees.
gryan stoutmantle | who gives this quest | quest giver westfall
Why does Stoutmantle send you to Lakeshire?

The People's Militia lacks underground informants within Westfall itself. Stoutmantle calls in an old personal favor from Wiley the Black, a rogue residing in Lakeshire's inn, hoping underworld contacts can reveal who leads the thieves.
why lakeshire | why go to redridge | why wiley

Wiley the Black is a rogue staying on the second floor of the Lakeshire Inn in Redridge Mountains. He owes Gryan Stoutmantle a favor, making him a useful conduit for underground rumors and criminal connections.
who is wiley | wiley lakeshire | wiley the black

The Defias Brotherhood is a ruthless criminal cartel wearing red masks that has seized control of Westfall's farms, roads, and abandoned mines, actively driving out homesteaders and challenging the authority of Stormwind.
defias brotherhood | what is defias | red bandana bandits

Wiley the Black is located upstairs on the second floor of the Lakeshire Inn, which sits near the bridge in the Redridge Mountains town of Lakeshire.
where is wiley | find wiley | wiley location
Does this quest involve any combat?
No. This initial step is entirely informational. You simply journey from Sentinel Hill in Westfall across Elwynn Forest to the inn in Lakeshire to make contact with Wiley.

Stoutmantle recognizes that formal soldiering cannot crack a criminal syndicate; it takes someone who understands shadows and street favors, leading directly to Wiley the Black.
The long journey from Westfall to Redridge highlights how deeply Stormwind's outer territories must rely on one another while the capital remains indifferent.
Why does Gryan Stoutmantle need an adventurer instead of his own People's Militia?

Gryan Stoutmantle's People's Militia is stretched thin just trying to defend Sentinel Hill and protect the few remaining farmers in Westfall. Stormwind refuses to send royal reinforcements, leaving the local defense desperately undermanned. Furthermore, Stoutmantle specifically needs an outsider capable of covert infiltration rather than recognizable local militia fighters who would be spotted immediately by Defias lookouts.

Ashenvale Outrunners is a Horde patrol-interception mission issued by Kuray'bin in Ashenvale. Night elf scouts have fanned out from Silverwing Outpost to gather intelligence on nearby Horde encampments, prompting a preemptive strike to keep the outpost's defenses hidden. By hunting down these stealthy scouts, the Horde blinds the local Alliance forces and discourages future incursions.

The forests of Ashenvale remain a contested frontier where every path and ridge is fiercely watched. Intelligence is as deadly as an axe, and reports reaching Kuray'bin confirm that night elf scouts known as Ashenvale Outrunners have slipped out from the Alliance stronghold at Silverwing Outpost. Operating in the dense wilderness east of their base and south of local Horde holdings, these scouts stalk the woodland paths to map out fortifications and track troop movements.

To prevent an organized assault, the Horde relies on eliminating enemy reconnaissance before it can return home. By hunting down the outrunners, Horde champions deny the commanders at Silverwing Outpost vital knowledge about troop strength and outpost perimeter defenses. Stripped of their forward eyes, the night elves are left disoriented and far less willing to risk aggressive maneuvers through the contested woodlands.

The quest is given by Kuray'bin, a Horde scout coordinator stationed in Ashenvale who works to track and counter night elf movements across the forest.
quest giver | who gives quest | kuray'bin quest

Neutralizing enemy outrunners turns the tables on night elf stealth, ensuring Horde infiltrators hold dominion over the shadows of the forest.
Every night elf scout cut down in Ashenvale protects local encampments and lumber operations from coordinated Alliance counter-offensives.
Why does Kuray'bin want the Ashenvale Outrunners killed?

Kuray'bin wants to blind the Alliance and prevent them from mounting an organized assault on Horde territory. The outrunners recently slipped out from Silverwing Outpost to prowl near Horde lines, and if they map out your camp's defenses and troop movements, an Alliance offensive is almost certain to follow. Eliminating them denies the enemy crucial battlefield intelligence.

While transporting a newly acquired goblin shredder from Ratchet to the Warsong Lumber Camp, the orc Gurda Ragescar lost the machine's operating manual to a sudden gust of wind. Stranded near Splintertree Post, she cannot run the complex engineering marvel without recovering the scattered pages.

The Warsong Clan relies heavily on steam-powered shredders bought from the goblins of the port of Ratchet to clear lumber across Ashenvale. Operating these delicate, noisy contraptions is far from intuitive for an ordinary orc warrior. When Gurda Ragescar made the journey north with a freshly purchased shredder, a sudden blast of wind tore the instruction booklet from her hands, scattering twelve fragile parchment leaves across the forest floor.

Because the wild winds swept the manual over the canopy, individual pages have drifted into the hands of wandering creatures, cultists, and forest denizens across the entire region. Without all three gathered chapters, the complex machine remains an inert block of steel and whirring sawblades, leaving Gurda stranded along the road to Splintertree Post unable to report for logging duty.
Gurda Ragescar is a Horde laborer tasked with ferrying a goblin shredder from the merchant port of Ratchet up into Ashenvale to join the logging efforts of the Warsong Lumber Camp.
gurda | ragescar | who is the quest giver

Goblin engineering is famously finicky and counterintuitive, reliant on volatile boilers, intricate pressure valves, and complex levers. Even an eager orc cannot safely operate the contraption without reading the manufacturer's manual.

Manual labor and warrior traditions leave little patience for detailed goblin paperwork, making Gurda's exasperation with lost technical sheets deeply relatable.

She was entrusted to bring the expensive machine back from Ratchet to report for duty at the Warsong Lumber Camp. Without the manual, she has no idea how to drive it, and abandoning the vehicle in the wilderness to search the forest on foot would leave valuable Horde equipment undefended.

Protect Kaya is a Horde escort quest in the Stonetalon Mountains. After discovering Kaya Flathoof held captive by hostile Grimtotem tauren, adventurers guide her through dangerous mountain trails to reach Camp Aparaje. Returning word of her survival brings immense relief to her anxious father, Makaba Flathoof.

The Stonetalon Mountains harbor bitter rivalries among the tauren, none sharper than the tension surrounding the treacherous Grimtotem clan. Deep within hostile territory, Kaya Flathoof was captured and held prisoner. Escaping on foot requires navigating winding trails flanked by opportunistic predators and watchful enemies, making an armed escort her only realistic hope of reaching friendly soil.

Camp Aparaje lies in the eastern Stonetalon Mountains, and Kaya knows her way home from there. She aims for the camp, confident that once she reaches it she can find her own way. Guiding her through the ambush-heavy paths ensures she avoids recapture before her captors realize she slipped away.

Awaiting news near the southeastern border of Stonetalon, Makaba Flathoof fears the absolute worst for his missing daughter. When runners arrive to deliver confirmation that Kaya safely reached Camp Aparaje, Makaba's despair turns to overwhelming gratitude toward the champions who stood between his child and her captors.
Kaya Flathoof is a young tauren who was captured by hostile Grimtotem forces in the Stonetalon Mountains. She relies on passing Horde adventurers to break her out and shepherd her to safe ground.

Thork at the Crossroads directs able Horde fighters north to Kadrak's watch tower near the Ashenvale border. Kadrak coordinates the Horde's expansion into the ancient forest and prepares incoming recruits for the ongoing skirmishes ahead.

While the Crossroads deals with quilboar, centaur, and local brigands, the Horde's broader territorial interests look north toward the thick forests of Ashenvale. Thork acts as an intermediary, directing seasoned fighters who have proven themselves in the central Barrens toward the northern border tower manned by Kadrak.

Kadrak oversees the southern approach to Ashenvale, organizing reinforcements for the Horde's foothold across the border. With new encampments like Splintertree Post and the outpost along the Zoram Strand, the Horde is actively consolidating its presence in the timber-rich woodlands despite fierce resistance from the native night elves.

Thork is an orc officer stationed at the Crossroads in the Barrens. He helps coordinate local defense efforts and marshals promising adventurers toward regional war efforts like the campaign in Ashenvale.

By reporting to Kadrak, soldiers are marshaled to support forward encampments like Splintertree Post and the Zoram Strand.
A Call to the Northern Front

In the craggy pass of Malaka'jin, the orc Darn Talongrip keeps an eye on the Horde's southern and mountain frontiers. Yet the greatest military pressure lies northward in the ancient forests of Ashenvale, where night elf sentinels clash incessantly with Warsong lumber gatherers. Recognizing blooded fighters passing through Stonetalon, Darn directs capable recruits toward the northern Barrens watch tower to assist with ongoing campaigns.

Positioned squarely upon the northern threshold where the arid savannah meets the verdant canopy of Ashenvale, the orc Kadrak oversees Horde troop movement into contested territory. The Horde is aggressively securing its foothold, maintaining outposts at both the western Zoram Strand and Splintertree Post to the north. Kadrak serves as the vital junction for coordinating supplies, troops, and urgent reports across these embattled forest lines.

Assigned by Kadrak at the border watchtower between the northern Barrens and Ashenvale, this mission tasks couriers with coordinating field intel across the contested forest. Adventurers must deliver standing orders and collect front-line reconnaissance from outriders stationed near Azshara, Splintertree Post, and the Zoram Strand.

Standing atop the fortified watchtower on the northern edge of the Barrens, Kadrak oversees movement through the narrow mountain canyon leading into Ashenvale. For the Horde, securing access through this pass is crucial: the arid steppes cannot provide the vast timber supplies required by Orgrimmar, forcing the Warsong clan to push deep into ancient elven woodlands. Keeping scattered forward patrols supplied and synchronized requires reliable couriers capable of dodging night elf ambushes along Ashenvale's treacherous wilderness trails.

The mission traces an arc across the breadth of the ancient forest. To the far west on the misty coastline of the Zoram Strand, a Warsong runner keeps watch over naga activity and coastal threats near Zoram'gar Outpost. Deeper inland at Splintertree Post, a scout coordinates defense against persistent Sentinel raids. Farther east along the winding road toward the shattered ruins of Azshara, an outrider monitors eastern approaches. Securing updates from all three posts provides Kadrak with a cohesive view of night elf troop movements and frontier vulnerabilities.
The mission begins with Kadrak, an orc officer stationed in the wooden watchtower guarding the mountain pass on the border between the northern Barrens and southern Ashenvale.

Torek's Assault is a direct Horde raid launched from the wilds of Ashenvale against the nearby night elf garrison at Silverwing Outpost. Led by the orc raider Torek under orders from Splintertree Post, the strike aims to crush local Sentinel resistance and slay their commander, Duriel Moonfire. It marks one of the most brazen, bloody skirmishes in the ongoing war for Ashenvale's borders.
